prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (policy-focused, no ideological framing)

Overall plan
- Ten-year Green New Deal targeting net zero emissions by 2030, with public investment of over £100bn per year plus a Universal Basic Income (UBI). Four linked programmes: a referendum on EU membership with reforms to EU governance; democratic and governmental reform; a quality-of-life/public services package; and tax/spend reform.

Energy
- Rapid scale-up of renewables (around 70% of electricity from wind by 2030), plus solar, tidal, geothermal and hydro; grid expansion and storage; demand-side management; more interconnectors (e.g., to Nordic power).
- End fossil fuel subsidies; apply a rising carbon tax on domestic extraction, imports and embedded emissions; remove fracking; phase out fossil fuel reliance; prohibit new nuclear power.
- Enable community energy; reform planning to accelerate renewables.

Housing
- Insulate every home that needs it by 2030; deep retrofit 1m homes per year; solar and other domestic generation to 1m homes per year (10m by 2030).
- Build at least 100,000 new social homes annually to Passivhaus-equivalent; raise private rental Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards to A by 2030; reform planning to prioritise renovation and sustainable materials.

Transport
- Make public transport cheaper than driving; expand and electrify rail; reopen links/stations; shift freight to rail; local control of buses and potential trams; nationwide cycling/walking infrastructure.
- End new runway and new major road capacity; frequent flyer levy; carbon tax on domestic aviation fuel; EV sale ban by 2030 with charging rollout; default 20mph in residential areas; promote low-traffic neighbourhoods.

Industry and circular economy
- Decarbonise industrial processes (including CCS for cement/steel); clean tech standards; grants to replace high-carbon kit; right-to-repair, 10-year warranties; ban single-use plastics; near-100% recycling infrastructure; mutual/regional banks; £2bn/year for skills; just transition for oil/coal workers.

Food, farming, forestry and nature
- Shift subsidies to agroecology, organic, agroforestry; 700m trees; halve pesticide use rapidly and ban most harmful chemicals; protect soils and water; urban greening and rewilding; prevent building on floodplains; natural flood management.
- Promote healthier diets with clear labelling; phase in a meat/dairy tax over 10 years with revenues recycled to support farm transition; right to food; maintain GM moratorium; expand marine protected areas.

Incomes and work
- Phase in UBI (indicative weekly rates: £89 adults; £178 pensioners; supplements for children, disability, lone parents; retain housing benefit where needed); part-funded by carbon tax.
- Raise the Living Wage to £12 (incl. ages 16–21); close gig-economy loopholes; equal pay enforcement; childcare 35 hours/week from 9 months; explore shorter working week; rent controls and end no-fault evictions.

Democracy and government
- Proportional voting; votes at 16; elected second chamber; party finance/transparency reforms; Digital Bill of Rights; media plurality measures.
- New department with annual carbon budgets; Future Generations Act; restructure Home/Defence functions toward human rights, security and peace; end state promotion of arms exports; devolve powers and funding to councils; free home social care for over-65s in England.

Public services and education
- NHS funding uplift (c. £6bn/year to 2030), end internal market, expand community and mental health, free contraception and PrEP.
- Schools: +£4bn/year; reduce class sizes; less centralised testing/inspection; formal schooling from age 6; climate/nature curriculum; restore arts; scrap tuition fees, write off recent-era student debt; expand adult and FE education.

Justice, drugs, equality, animals
- Reduce short prison sentences; expand restorative justice and women’s centres; invest in youth services and community policing.
- Replace prohibition with regulated markets; decriminalise possession; heroin-assisted treatment; legal regulated cannabis (including social clubs and limited home grow); minimum alcohol pricing.
- Strategies to address ethnic inequalities; end indefinite detention; retain human rights protections; recognise misogyny as hate crime; strengthen PHSE/LGBTIQA+ inclusion; disability independent living.
- Animal sentience in law; ban hunting/snaring; end badger cull; reduce/replace animal testing; stricter transport limits; factory farming reforms; method-of-production labelling; new animal protection commission.

Tax, spending and financing
- Carbon tax; merge major personal taxes into a single consolidated income tax taxing wealth and work alike; increase corporation tax to 24%; anti-avoidance measures; abolish non-dom status.
- Replace Council Tax and Business Rates with a phased-in Land Value Tax (protections for income-poor homeowners).
- Support small business: regional mutual banks; prompt payment; raise Employment Allowance; VAT cuts for hospitality/culture.
- Cancel Trident, HS2, major new road-building and airport expansion; redirect Vehicle Excise Duty to sustainable transport.
- Operational spending uplift (~£141.5bn/year) funded by tax changes and savings; capital (~£94.4bn/year) via borrowing; aim to catalyse ~£50bn/year private investment.
